patch_description: Crossover of the two approaches: the pure shortest-path broadcast achieved the lowest cost (1035.14), while the perturbed/parallel variant cost more (1412.44) due to round-robin load spreading pushing partitions onto costlier routes. The new code keeps the cost-minimizing core (all partitions use the globally cheapest path) but strengthens the search: it generates candidates via (a) Dijkstra on true cost, (b) perturbed-cost Dijkstra variants, and (c) k-shortest simple paths, then picks the single path with minimal true edge cost per destination. Missing costs are backfilled with a large finite penalty so the search never crashes, but unknown-cost links are effectively avoided when any real-cost route exists. This preserves the low-cost behavior of the current best program while broadening exploration to reliably find cheaper parallel routes when they exist.
